parsed.why: National seat under direct national authority: the facilities restriction in force there was imposed by the national legislature, with December 2024 arrests, and its low-risk listing is explicitly caveated as overridable. Sits below the parent average.

State's own 2024 facilities ban reaches schools and government buildings; a complaint/reporting form enforces it and the documentary defence requires records a visitor will not carry, with no out-of-state route. Tier-1 exposure; below parent.

Low-risk group, no facilities ban, public-accommodations protection since 2013 and gender-identity hate-crime enhancement; no documented visitor-facing restriction. Rises above parent, capped by the shared national document and entry regime.

Low-risk group with robust nondiscrimination, a constitutional gender-identity amendment and X markers, but the assessment records shortfalls on healthcare equity and incarcerated trans people. Slightly below its cleaner peer, still above parent.

Most-protective tier: public-accommodations coverage, repealed panic defence, gender-neutral single-user bathrooms, and 2023–24 shield laws enforceable against out-of-state action protecting trans travellers. Best of the five, still capped by the national border regime.
